entries.text_de:
British Museum Cotton Titus A XXVII. Hinter Galfrid von Monmouth folgt f. 88 ein ursprünglich gesonderter Band von zwei Händen um 1225.

Die erste schreibt den Quadripartitus von Arg. 1 an, u. S. 5326; f. 90b Cnut, u. S. 279; f. 104b Af-Ine, u. S. 17; f. 121. 121b I. II As, u. S. 147. 151; f. 123b Episc, u. S. 477; f. 124 Norðleod, Mirce, Að, Had, u. S. 459—465; f. 125 Blas, Forf, u. S. 389; f. 125b Hu, u. S. 192; f. 126. 127. 127b. 128b IV. V. III. VI As, u. S. 171. 167. 170. 173; f. 132 Ordal, u. S. 386; f. 132b AGu, u. S. 127; f. 133 App AGu, u. S. 394; f. 133 EGu, u. S. 129; f. 134b I. II Ew, u. S. 139; f. 135b I. II Em, u. S. 185; f. 136b Swer, u. S. 397; f. 137b Wif, u. S. 443; f. 138 Wer, u. S. 393; f. 138b. 139 I. III Atr, u. S. 217. 228; f. 140 Pax, Wal, u. S. 391 f.; f. 141. 142b IV. II Atr, u. S. 232. 221; f. 143 Duns, u. S. 375; f. 144 VII Atr, u. S. 260; f. 145 Iudex, u. S. 474; f. 145b II. III Eg, u. S. 195; f. 146b III Em, u. S. 190; f. 147b Wl lad, u. S. 483; f. 147b Wl art, u. S. 486 [dies wohl nicht aus Quadr.]; f. 148b Geþyncðo, u. S. 457; f. 149 Rect, u. S. 444; f. 151 [Quadr. II] Praef., u. S. 542; f. 152 CHn cor, u. S. 521; f. 153b—158b Quadr. II 4—18, u. S. 544 ff.; f. 159 Hn com, u. S. 524.

F. 159b andere Hand In Cn, u. S. 612. Hierfür ist Cb verwandt.

Es folgen f. 174 Marbod: Gedichte über Steine.

Die Randnotiz eines Lesers auf f. 49b zu Galfrid III 7 verräth Interesse für Thanet. Und dieser Band enthält die Texte, die der Londoner Andreas Horn in Co nachtrug und im Liber S. Augustini Cant. (apud S. Aug. Cant.) gefunden zu haben behauptet. Ich glaube daher, dass T Saint Austin’s zu Canterbury gehörte.

Entweder war T im 17. Jh. im Besitze des Sir Simonds d’Ewes, oder dieser besass eine Schwesterhandschrift des Quadripartitus, aus welcher erstens Somner1 VII Atr und Iudex citirt und zweitens Harley 5962 copirt: Af-Ine, As, AGu, Ew, I. III. IV VII Atr, Duns, Iudex, Eg, Em; hier heisst die Vorlage pervetusta.
entries.text_en:
British Museum Cotton Titus A XXVII. After Geoffrey of Monmouth there follows at f. 88 an originally separate volume in two hands of c. 1225.

The first writes the Quadripartitus from Arg. 1 onwards, below, p. 5326; f. 90b Cnut, below, p. 279; f. 104b Af-Ine, below, p. 17; f. 121. 121b I. II As, below, pp. 147. 151; f. 123b Episc, below, p. 477; f. 124 Norðleod, Mirce, Að, Had, below, pp. 459—465; f. 125 Blas, Forf, below, p. 389; f. 125b Hu, below, p. 192; f. 126. 127. 127b. 128b IV. V. III. VI As, below, pp. 171. 167. 170. 173; f. 132 Ordal, below, p. 386; f. 132b AGu, below, p. 127; f. 133 App AGu, below, p. 394; f. 133 EGu, below, p. 129; f. 134b I. II Ew, below, p. 139; f. 135b I. II Em, below, p. 185; f. 136b Swer, below, p. 397; f. 137b Wif, below, p. 443; f. 138 Wer, below, p. 393; f. 138b. 139 I. III Atr, below, pp. 217. 228; f. 140 Pax, Wal, below, p. 391 f.; f. 141. 142b IV. II Atr, below, pp. 232. 221; f. 143 Duns, below, p. 375; f. 144 VII Atr, below, p. 260; f. 145 Iudex, below, p. 474; f. 145b II. III Eg, below, p. 195; f. 146b III Em, below, p. 190; f. 147b Wl lad, below, p. 483; f. 147b Wl art, below, p. 486 [this probably not from Quadr.]; f. 148b Geþyncðo, below, p. 457; f. 149 Rect, below, p. 444; f. 151 [Quadr. II] Praef., below, p. 542; f. 152 CHn cor, below, p. 521; f. 153b—158b Quadr. II 4—18, below, p. 544 ff.; f. 159 Hn com, below, p. 524.

F. 159b, another hand, In Cn, below, p. 612. For this Cb is related.

There follow at f. 174 Marbod: poems on stones.

A reader's marginal note on f. 49b to Geoffrey III 7 betrays an interest in Thanet. And this volume contains the texts which the Londoner Andrew Horn added in Co and claims to have found in the Liber S. Augustini Cant. (apud S. Aug. Cant.). I therefore believe that T belonged to Saint Austin's at Canterbury.

Either T was in the 17th century in the possession of Sir Simonds d’Ewes, or the latter owned a sister MS of the Quadripartitus, from which, firstly, Somner1 cited VII Atr and Iudex and, secondly, Harley 5962 copied: Af-Ine, As, AGu, Ew, I. III. IV VII Atr, Duns, Iudex, Eg, Em; here the exemplar is called pervetusta.

wormald.other_contents: By the 14th century set between Geoffrey of Monmouth and pseudo-historical pieces incl. 'Prester John's' letter to Emperor Manuel; legal section originally distinct (p. 238).
wormald.overview: A Quadripartitus copy of about 1200, later at St Augustine's, Canterbury, representing the fourth of the five stages Wormald identifies, before the final M/Hk arrangement (it still places III Edmund and the run of texts that begins with Alfred–Guthrum and ends with Wergeld differently). By the fourteenth century it had been bound up with Geoffrey of Monmouth's history and other tales of wonder; its legal part, originally separate, was supplemented with related texts such as the Instituta Cnuti.
wormald.key_quote: T (5), otherwise perhaps the latest manuscript, was also given a historical slant by the fourteenth century (p. 238)
wormald.doubts: GUIDE: Liebermann dates T c. 1225, Wormald s. xii/xiii (p. 237) — a modest difference (moved from liebermann_superseded).
